---
title: "Fit multiple fisheries and surveys"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE),
    file.path(guide_root, "NAMESPACE"))
} else {
  c(list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"),
    pattern = "[.](R|rdb|rdx)$", full.names = TRUE),
    system.file("NAMESPACE", package = "tinyAM"))
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = TRUE,
  cache.extra = list(package = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
    R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
    mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")),
    sources = unname(tools::md5sum(source_files)),
    inputs = sim_cod_obs, truth = sim_cod_truth))
```

Different fishing gears remove different parts of a shared population. Surveys
also differ in coverage and selectivity. tinyAM represents these differences
with fleet-specific fishing mortality and survey-specific catchability, while
retaining one population and natural-mortality surface.

This example uses [SimSurvey](https://paulregular.github.io/SimSurvey/) data
loosely based on 3Ps cod: three active fisheries, an offshore RV-like survey and
a coastal Sentinel-gillnet-like survey. The [dataset help](../reference/sim_cod_obs.html)
documents their generation and separate truth tables.

## Inspect the input keys

```{r inputs}
dat <- sim_cod_obs
check_tam_data(dat)
head(dat$catch)
head(dat$index)
```

Catch has a complete year–age grid within each `fleet`. An unavailable catch is
`NA`; it does not imply a closure. Each index row identifies `survey` and
`samp_time`. Both simulated surveys observe the population at the beginning of
each modeled year (`samp_time = 0`): this specifies timing, not sampling effort.

F covariates belong in catch, q covariates in index, and recruitment/N/M
covariates in `pop_covariates`. Here `mean_length` is the assumed-known population
mean length at age in cm, not a mean calculated from selected fish.

The Sentinel-like survey samples a coastal band more densely than the RV-like
survey samples offshore. Its dome-shaped selection contrasts with ascending
RV selection. Both use swept-area sampling; the Sentinel-like program does not
reproduce net saturation or literal fish-per-net CPUE.

```{r footprints, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap="Survey footprints on the synthetic grid. The northern edge represents the coast; grey cells are outside each survey's footprint."}
local({
  old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.8, 2.2, 0.8),
             mgp = c(2.8, 0.8, 0), cex = 0.85)
  on.exit(par(old))
  grid <- sim_cod_truth$footprint
  for (survey in c("RV", "Sentinel")) {
    selected <- grid[[survey]]
    plot(grid$x, grid$y, asp = 1, pch = 15, cex = 0.45,
      col = "grey90", xlab = "East-west (km)", ylab = "North-south (km)",
      main = if (survey == "RV") "RV-like" else "Sentinel-gillnet-like")
    points(grid$x[selected], grid$y[selected], pch = 15, cex = 0.45,
    col = tam_cols()[if (survey == "RV") 1 else 7])
  }
})
```

Catch inputs are expanded monitoring estimates, not true catches or raw age
sample counts. Genuine zeros remain in the inputs but are excluded from the
lognormal likelihood. Missing biological samples are not zero catches.

This introductory scenario uses a fixed spatial pattern, a 20-by-20 grid, and
log-scale SDs of 0.03 for length at age and 0.1 for total mortality, compared
with 0.1 and 0.2 in the original SimSurvey paper. Static coverage keeps regional
availability approximately constant; whole-fish rounding can cause small changes.

## Describe each fleet within one formula

`for_fleet()` gives each fleet its own scale and curve. Inner formulas include
intercepts, so use outer `~ 0 +` to avoid an extra common baseline.

```{r fleet-formula, cache=TRUE}
fishing <- ~ 0 +
  for_fleet("Trawl", ~ logistic(mean_length)) +
  for_fleet("Longline", ~ logistic(mean_length)) +
  for_fleet("Gillnet", ~ double_logistic(mean_length))
```

Trawl and longline curves ascend; the gillnet curve can decline. The generator
selects individual lengths, whereas the fitted curves use mean length at age.
These are approximations: a nonlinear curve at mean length need not equal mean
selectivity. Realized F also reflects access, capture and depletion.

```{r selection, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap="Generating selectivity curves. Dashed lines identify surveys; solid lines identify fisheries."}
local({
  curves <- sim_cod_truth$selectivity
  components <- c("Trawl", "Longline", "Gillnet", "RV", "Sentinel")
  colors <- tam_cols()[c(1, 2, 3, 6, 7)]
  line_types <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2)
  plot(range(curves$length), c(0, 1), type = "n",
    xlab = "Length (cm)", ylab = "Selectivity")
  for (i in seq_along(components)) {
    d <- curves[curves$component == components[i], ]
    lines(d$length, d$selectivity, col = colors[i], lty = line_types[i], lwd = 2)
  }
  legend("bottomright", legend = components, col = colors, lty = line_types,
    lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
})
```

The raw double-logistic product is not peak-normalized; its scale is not
automatically maximum F. See [scopes](../reference/for_fleet.html) and
[double-logistic help](../reference/double_logistic.html) for its definition.

## Give surveys their own relationships

```{r survey-formula, cache=TRUE}
catchability <- ~ 0 +
  for_survey("RV", ~ logistic(mean_length)) +
  for_survey("Sentinel", ~ double_logistic(mean_length))
```

Each survey has a separate q scale and shape. With the default log link, q is
positive and can exceed one. Here it includes the fraction of the population
inside the footprint. Changing regional availability would require further
assumptions; it is deliberately simplified in this example.

## Compare assumptions about natural mortality

The supplied `M0` is a known baseline from the simulation settings, not realized
M. Average it geometrically within four age blocks so that each block has one
reference value per year.

```{r mortality-reference, cache=TRUE}
breaks <- c(1, 4, 6, 11, 21)
dat$pop_covariates$M0_block <- with(dat$pop_covariates,
  exp(ave(log(M0), year, cut(age, breaks, right = FALSE), FUN = mean)))
```

```{r reference-M, cache=TRUE, dependson=c("fleet-formula", "survey-formula", "mortality-reference"), results='hide'}
reference_M <- fit_tam(
  dat, ages = 1:20,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = fishing,
                   sd_form = ~ fleet, mean_ages = 5:10),
  M_settings = list(process = "off", mu_supplied = ~ M0_block,
                   age_breaks = breaks, mean_ages = 5:10),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ fleet),
  index_settings = list(q_form = catchability, sd_form = ~ survey)
)
```

Now allow M to vary around those same block baselines:

```{r variable-M, cache=TRUE, dependson="reference-M", results='hide'}
variable_M <- update(reference_M, M_settings = list(process = "ar1"))
```

```{r checks}
check_tam(reference_M, variable_M)
```

The models differ only in the M process. Both use exact cohort survival,
random-walk recruitment and separate AR1 F processes. M blocks share actual M;
F innovations are independent between fleets, conditional on shared parameters.
SD formulas distinguish fleet
and survey precision. Average F/M use ages 5–10. The terminal age 20 is a plus
group; the generator's finite-age losses remain a small approximation to check.

Allowing M variation is closer to this generator than setting M equal to its
baseline, but neither model is exact. Their intervals condition on known
biology and baseline M; they do not establish that M is identifiable in real data.
The generator partitions pre-generated total deaths, connecting fleet F and
remaining M variation; the fitted fleet and M processes have separate densities.

The shared population experiences total fishing mortality,

\[
F^{\mathrm{total}}_{t,a}=\sum_f F_{t,a,f},
\qquad Z_{t,a}=M_{t,a}+F^{\mathrm{total}}_{t,a}.
\]

Each fleet's Baranov prediction uses its own F and this common Z. Catch weights
determine yield; stock weights determine biomass/SSB. Catch numbers are in
thousand fish and weights in kg, giving biomass in tonnes.

## Inspect fleets, surveys and the common population

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
vis_tam(ReferenceM = reference_M, AR1M = variable_M, open_file = FALSE)
```

Explore the [simulated-cod dashboard](../examples/simulated-cod/index.html)
to inspect the example fits and diagnostics.

Start with each fleet under **Fisheries**, then inspect both **Surveys** before
population trends. **Aggregate fishery** shows total yield without inventing
aggregate standardized residuals.

```{r quantities}
ssb <- get_ssb(ReferenceM = reference_M, AR1M = variable_M)
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2), ylab = "SSB (tonnes)",
           add_buttons = FALSE) |>
  plotly::add_lines(data = sim_cod_truth$annual, x = ~year, y = ~SSB,
    inherit = FALSE, name = "Generating SSB",
    line = list(color = "#333333", dash = "dot"),
    hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y} tonnes<extra>Generating SSB</extra>") |>
  add_plot_buttons()
plot_matrix(get_f(variable_M))
```

The dotted line is known SSB, without a confidence interval. The table measures
relative error, `(estimate - truth) / truth`, across years and at the terminal
year; mean absolute relative error prevents errors of opposing signs from canceling.

```{r ssb-errors, echo=FALSE}
comparison <- merge(ssb, sim_cod_truth$annual[c("year", "SSB")], by = "year")
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 2L * nrow(sim_cod_truth$annual),
  !anyDuplicated(comparison[c("model", "year")]))
comparison$relative_error <- (comparison$est - comparison$SSB) / comparison$SSB
errors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("ReferenceM", "AR1M"), function(model) {
  d <- comparison[comparison$model == model, ]
  data.frame(Model = model, `Mean SSB (tonnes)` = mean(d$est),
    `Mean RE (%)` = 100 * mean(d$relative_error),
    `Mean ARE (%)` = 100 * mean(abs(d$relative_error)),
    `Terminal RE (%)` = 100 * d$relative_error[which.max(d$year)],
    check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(errors, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
population <- tidy_pop(variable_M)
secondary <- vapply(c(abundance = "N", recruitment = "recruitment"), function(column) {
  table <- population[[if (column == "N") "abundance" else "recruitment"]]
  position <- match(table$year, sim_cod_truth$annual$year)
  100 * mean(table$est / sim_cod_truth$annual[[column]][position] - 1)
}, numeric(1))
```

These compare historical estimates with truth for one selected teaching
realization, not forecast skill, simulation-study bias or coverage.
Mean errors for AR1M abundance and recruitment are
`r sprintf("%.1f%% and %.1f%%", secondary[["abundance"]], secondary[["recruitment"]])`.
Agreement in SSB does not guarantee recovery of every population quantity.
`get_f()` returns total F; fleet-specific F is in `tidy_pop(variable_M)$F_fleet`.
Use generating truth to evaluate results, not to alter observations.

As a further hypothesis, remove age-dependent q while retaining survey scales:

```{r flat-q, eval=FALSE}
flat_q <- update(variable_M, index_settings = list(q_form = ~ survey))
```

```{r dashboard-export, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
dashboard_cache <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_FITS")
if (nzchar(dashboard_cache)) {
  if (!nzchar(guide_root)) stop("Set TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT to the checkout when exporting guide fits.")
  source_paths <- c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$")),
    "NAMESPACE")
  dir.create(dirname(dashboard_cache), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(models = list(ReferenceM = reference_M, AR1M = variable_M),
    inputs = sim_cod_obs, truth = sim_cod_truth,
    background = paste("### Simulated cod fisheries and surveys",
      "Teaching data generated with SimSurvey: three active fleets, two regional surveys, and one closed population. Both fits use known biology and a reference M baseline; they differ in whether M has AR1 deviations.",
      "### SSB comparison with generating truth",
      paste(knitr::kable(errors, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"),
      "Errors describe this selected realization, not simulation-study bias or coverage. Abundance and recruitment can differ substantially even when SSB agrees. See the [guide](https://paulregular.github.io/tinyAM/articles/multiple-fisheries-surveys.html) for the assumptions and additional comparisons.",
      sep = "\n\n"),
    sources = setNames(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(guide_root, source_paths))), source_paths),
    versions = c(tinyAM = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
      R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
      mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")))), dashboard_cache)
}
```
